# PCSX2 recipes

<!-- Generated by `coney-tools pcsx2 recipe render` from research/pcsx2-recipes.toml. Do not edit. -->

Each recipe is one thing an engineer often needs to do in the original running in PCSX2: find a human, move one, change
a field, call one of the game's functions or a script binding, load a checkpoint. Every recipe has been run in PCSX2 and
says when, on which copy and from which state; each names the Ghidra address that justifies it and the research page
that explains it. The list is generated from `research/pcsx2-recipes.toml` by `coney-tools pcsx2 recipe render`; edit
that file, never these pages. The recipes are in groups, one page each; this page lists every recipe under its group and
links to its section.

Run a recipe on a copy you hold a claim on ([Driving PCSX2](research-tools.md#driving-pcsx2)): `coney-tools pcsx2 claim
--agent ID`, `coney-tools pcsx2 launch --agent ID STATE`, then `coney-tools pcsx2 recipe run NAME --copy COPY --agent ID
--arg name=value`. `recipe list` lists them and `recipe show NAME` prints one. The runner talks to the copy's PINE port
(and its debug server for the emulation steps), so the `pcsx2` MCP server must be connected in `mode: "debug"`, which
leaves PINE free. It checks first that the copy runs, that you hold its claim, that the emulation is running or paused
as the recipe needs, and that the running state holds every patch the recipe names: a patch goes into a copy of a state
with `coney-tools pcsx2 prepare-state SOURCE OUT --patch NAME ...` before PCSX2 starts on it.

A run that backs a research claim is recorded: add `--record --state ID` (the library state the copy started from, or
`unknown`) and a good run writes `research/runs/<id>.toml` with the numbers it showed, for the page to cite as
`confirmed (runtime), run <id>` ([Run records](research-evidence.md#run-records)).

Start from the shared state library rather than driving to the same place again: `coney-tools pcsx2 states list` shows
the saved places ([PCSX2 states](pcsx2-states.md)) and `coney-tools pcsx2 states use ID --copy COPY --agent ID --launch`
starts your copy on one. A recipe that needs a particular scene names its state among its preconditions (`recipe run`
prints it; the runner cannot tell which state the copy was started from).

Many recipes call the game through the `call-brains` call hook (`research/traces/patches/hooks-core.toml`): the runner
writes a function address and its arguments into the call block, and the game makes the call on its own thread at the
start of the next brains update. The `lua` recipe and the recipes built on it run a Lua chunk in the level's script
state the same way, so every script binding (`HuCreate`, `GiveMoney`, `MenuLoadLevel`, ...) can be used as a level
script uses it; [the script bindings](../references/bindings/index.md) list them with their arguments.

**Input: prefer recordings.** For runtime evidence that depends on input, drive the original with a PCSX2 input
recording (`pcsx2 record --recording`, [Input recordings](research-tools.md#input-recordings)): it replays the same pad
frame by frame. The `scripted-pad` recipes are for closed-loop drivers that decide each input from what the game shows,
which a recording cannot do.

## Finding humans

- [humans](pcsx2-recipes/finding-humans.md#humans){#humans}: List every human in use: table address, handle index, name,
  player number, position and heading.
- [find-player](pcsx2-recipes/finding-humans.md#find-player){#find-player}: The player's human (player number 0) and its
  tables: record, per-player record, brain and transform.
- [find-human](pcsx2-recipes/finding-humans.md#find-human){#find-human}: A human by name, with the same tables as
  find-player.

## Moving and editing humans

- [position](pcsx2-recipes/moving-and-editing-humans.md#position){#position}: Read a human's position, heading, speed
  and gait.
- [teleport](pcsx2-recipes/moving-and-editing-humans.md#teleport){#teleport}: Move a human to x, y, z and turn it to a
  heading (degrees), by writing its transform.
- [drop-human](pcsx2-recipes/moving-and-editing-humans.md#drop-human){#drop-human}: Teleport a human high above a point
  and let it fall: read its height as it drops and where it lands.
- [health](pcsx2-recipes/moving-and-editing-humans.md#health){#health}: Read a human's health, maximum, power, stamina
  and rage.
- [set-health](pcsx2-recipes/moving-and-editing-humans.md#set-health){#set-health}: Set a human's health (record +0x144,
  s16).
- [set-rage](pcsx2-recipes/moving-and-editing-humans.md#set-rage){#set-rage}: Fill (or empty) a human's rage meter
  (human +0x650, s32).
- [brain](pcsx2-recipes/moving-and-editing-humans.md#brain){#brain}: A human's AI: brain type, gang, goal stack (type
  ids), target and whether it is suspended.
- [held-object](pcsx2-recipes/moving-and-editing-humans.md#held-object){#held-object}: What a human holds: the handle in
  its hand (+0x338) and the object being picked up (+0x33c).

## Spawning

- [spawn-human](pcsx2-recipes/spawning.md#spawn-human){#spawn-human}: Create a human in front of the player, of the type
  and gang of a human already there (a pedestrian or a gang member).

## The crew

- [crew](pcsx2-recipes/the-crew.md#crew){#crew}: Read a war chief's crew: the gang's tactic and the command it belongs
  to, the command bytes, and each member's goals.
- [crew-command](pcsx2-recipes/the-crew.md#crew-command){#crew-command}: Give the crew a Warrior command from the
  script's side (IssueWarriorCommand), then read back the tactic and the members' goals.
- [crew-command-menu](pcsx2-recipes/the-crew.md#crew-command-menu){#crew-command-menu}: Give the crew a Warrior command
  through the pad, as a player does: hold R2, push the right stick to a slot, let go.
- [spawn-crew](pcsx2-recipes/the-crew.md#spawn-crew){#spawn-crew}: Add a Warrior to the war chief's crew: create one
  next to the player, in the player's gang, and read the crew back.

## Player state

- [inventory](pcsx2-recipes/player-state.md#inventory){#inventory}: A player's inventory counts: flash, money, spray
  paint, handcuffs, cuff keys and loot.
- [give-item](pcsx2-recipes/player-state.md#give-item){#give-item}: Give player 1 money or any inventory item through
  the game's own path (callbacks and limits included).
- [stats](pcsx2-recipes/player-state.md#stats){#stats}: Player 1's statistics: the score and the six category counters'
  first words.

## Input

- [pad](pcsx2-recipes/input.md#pad){#pad}: Hold buttons and both sticks on player 1's pad for some updates, then let go
  (closed-loop drivers).
- [stick-magnitude](pcsx2-recipes/input.md#stick-magnitude){#stick-magnitude}: Make full-deflection stick input read as
  a chosen magnitude, by rewriting the stick table's ends.
- [puppet-command](pcsx2-recipes/input.md#puppet-command){#puppet-command}: Make an AI human act on a command id for one
  update (attack, grab, block), as a puppet.

## Calling the game

- [call](pcsx2-recipes/calling-the-game.md#call){#call}: Make the game call one of its own functions with up to six
  integer or pointer arguments.
- [lua](pcsx2-recipes/calling-the-game.md#lua){#lua}: Run a Lua chunk in the level's script state, as a level script
  would: any script binding, any global.
- [lua-globals](pcsx2-recipes/calling-the-game.md#lua-globals){#lua-globals}: List the script's global variables (the
  mission script's state) whose names hold a pattern.
- [human-event](pcsx2-recipes/calling-the-game.md#human-event){#human-event}: Send a game event (an event record with an
  id) to a human: its script handler, its gang, then its brain.
- [uncuff](pcsx2-recipes/calling-the-game.md#uncuff){#uncuff}: Start freeing a cuffed human by the mash, as triangle
  does, and read where the freer and the cuffed human stand.

## Levels and missions

- [where](pcsx2-recipes/levels-and-missions.md#where){#where}: Which level and checkpoint the game is in, and the game
  state's address.
- [load-checkpoint](pcsx2-recipes/levels-and-missions.md#load-checkpoint){#load-checkpoint}: Reload a level at a
  checkpoint, as the story does after a save or a death: SetCheckPoint, then MenuLoadLevel.

## Emulation

- [pause](pcsx2-recipes/emulation.md#pause){#pause}: Pause emulation as a whole (the debug server's pause), to read or
  write a frozen moment.
- [resume](pcsx2-recipes/emulation.md#resume){#resume}: Resume emulation after pause or advance.
- [step](pcsx2-recipes/emulation.md#step){#step}: Run a number of frames from a pause, then pause again, and report how
  far the game's tick count moved.
